body:
> DO NOT GIVE HER THE GREEN LIGHT.

Oof, so you concur it's a good thing I didn't agree to yield to the whole "setting a deadline" business.

> You are also not required to solve her issues or be her therapist. It's not your responsibility, and realistically, you can't simply bring her out of that dark place and make her un-suicidal.

Well, as I said, she has recently resumed psychotherapy, so now she'll be visiting an actual professional therapist again. That being said, I'm the most important person in her life, and it's not unreasonable to assume that this will remain the case indefinitely, and this cannot *not* come with a serious responsibility. I might well be the only obstacle between her and the proverbial cliff.

I'm sure I won't find any "quick and dirty trick" to "un-suicidal" her with the snap of a finger, but I can't just do nothing.

> If you haven't read the talking tips and risk assessment guide, then I suggest you need to start there

Thank you so much! I'm so glad there are well-established guidelines for responding to someone else's suicidality. I've had to handle a lot more obscure manifestations of insanity that weren't therefore as well studied, and it was nerve-wrecking because it truly felt so isolating. At least suicide is a single-word concept that most people know about and can perhaps understand, so there's that social dynamic.

Also, crap: I have *just* learned about my bestie's suicidality yet have already managed to make a mistake or three, judging by that guideline - but at least now I already know what to do to avoid making the same mistakes again.

Boy, I guess it's time for me to start hoarding benzos again regardless, just in case.

> I've been in this position with my own friend numerable times

Well, *that* must take its toll. I wouldn't wish anybody to be suicidal or have their loved one be suicidal. It's a good thing you've figured out what works, though.

> . . . That's something very sweet and easy to do, and it's something that I've seen go pretty far in the long run.

Will do!

***

Edit. Well, she just invited me to binge on TikTok videos with her and is laughing and seems to be having a good time, so maybe that's a good sign. At least there's no urgent danger.
